identity.name: Principality of Wales
alt_names: Principality of Wales under the English Crown

land.text: Gwynedd, annexed after Dafydd's execution in 1283
Carmarthenshire and Cardiganshire under the Justiciar of South (West) Wales
'The Principality ceased to exist as a legal entity' with the Laws in Wales Acts 1535 and 1542

correction.text: the five counties of the Principality after the Statute of Rhuddlan: Anglesey, Merioneth and Caernarfon (Gwynedd and Conwy council areas), Cardigan and Carmarthen

keyframe_review.note: [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Flintshire is dropped: the Principality of Wales page says 'Another county, Flintshire, was created out of the lordships of Tegeingl, Hopedale and Maelor Saesneg and was administered with the Palatinate of Cheshire by the Justiciar of Chester', while the Statute's principality counties are Anglesey, Merionethshire and Caernarfonshire in the north and Carmarthenshire and Cardiganshire in the south; Flintshire belongs with the Crown of England (palatinate of Chester), not drawn here. The single 1283-1541 shape of the first version is split at the Glyndwr events. Earlier note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no English Principality (its Kingdom of England shapes cover Wales). Infobox: 'Dependent territory of England (1283-1542)'; no area. The nominal shape stands for the whole life; the Glyndwr years 1404-1409 are ledger events. Marcher lordships were 'for all practical purposes, not part of the principality'.

correction.text: Anglesey and Carmarthenshire, regained from Glyndwr

keyframe_review.note: [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Between 1404 and 1406 the whole Principality was in rebel hands (glyndwr-s-wales draws it; no shape here, which was a double fill of 39 H3 cells in 1404 and 17 in 1408). Anglesey: 'the resistance in Anglesey formally ended toward the end of 1406'; Carmarthenshire: 'By 1407 the English had recaptured Anglesey and large parts of south Wales' (Glyndwr Rising page).

correction.text: the five counties again: Aberystwyth surrendered in autumn 1408 and Harlech fell in February 1409

keyframe_review.note: [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] 'That autumn, Aberystwyth Castle surrendered' (1408) and 'February 1409: Harlech Castle falls' (Glyndwr Rising page); 'By 1409 the rebellion's last remaining castles of Harlech and Aberystwyth had been captured' (Owain page). The Principality is whole again from 1409 until the Laws in Wales Acts.

region.text: Anglesey, Merioneth and Caernarfon (Gwynedd, Conwy), the lands of Llywelyn's principality

ledger.note: 1283: Edward I annexes Wales. 'Edward I conquered the territories of Llywelyn ap Gruffudd and the other last remaining native Welsh princes' (1277-1283); Dafydd 'was captured and executed in 1283'; the Statute of Rhuddlan of 3 March 1284 'annexed and united' the principality to the English crown. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Flintshire dropped from the region (see the keyframe note): the Perfeddwlad's Flintshire went to the Crown as a county of the Justiciar of Chester.

1283: the Deheubarth lands become royal. 'Carmarthenshire and Cardiganshire fell under the Justiciar of South (West) Wales' (Statute of Rhuddlan, 1284). [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Consistent with deheubarth's 1197-1282 keyframe, which now keeps Ceredigion; marcher-lordships no longer records a loss of Ceredigion.

region.text: the whole Principality, in rebel hands from 1404

ledger.note: 1404: Owain Glyndwr takes Harlech and Aberystwyth. 'In 1404, Owain's forces took Aberystwyth Castle and Harlech Castle.' The page does not list what the Crown kept. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Flintshire dropped from the region.

region.text: Anglesey, where the rebels' resistance formally ended

ledger.note: 1406 (late): the Principality regains Anglesey. Owain page: 'the resistance in Anglesey formally ended toward the end of 1406' (the Glyndwr Rising page's lead says 'By 1407 the English had recaptured Anglesey').

region.text: Carmarthenshire, part of the large parts of south Wales recaptured

ledger.note: By 1407: 'the English had recaptured Anglesey and large parts of south Wales' (Glyndwr Rising page, lead); Carmarthen had been taken by Owain in 1403 and by the French and Welsh in 1405. The page names no date or county inside 1405-1407; Carmarthenshire is the researcher's reading of 'south Wales'.
1408: Aberystwyth regained. 'By 1408, the English regained Aberystwyth.' The Glyndwr Rising page: 'That autumn, Aberystwyth Castle surrendered' (1408), so the shape returns in 1409.

region.text: Gwynedd (Harlech) and Conwy, regained when Harlech fell

ledger.note: 1409 (February): Harlech falls. Glyndwr Rising page: 'February 1409: Harlech Castle falls', 'effectively ending Owain's territorial rule'; Owain page: 'By 1409 the rebellion's last remaining castles of Harlech and Aberystwyth had been captured'. Owain's wife and daughters were captured there. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Region narrowed to Gwynedd and Conwy: Anglesey (1406) and Carmarthenshire (1407) are separate gains and Flintshire is dropped.

region.text: the Principality, as a legal entity

ledger.note: 1542: the Principality ceases. 'The Principality ceased to exist as a legal entity' with the Laws in Wales Acts 1535 and 1542; the infobox gives 'Dependent territory of England (1283-1542)'; 'The implementation of the act was delayed until a more detailed act was used in 1543'.

wars.name: Welsh Revolt of 1294-1295
wars.outcome: A revolt against English rule; the Principality remained.
wars.note: The page gives the dates only in the infobox.

wars.name: Glyndwr Rising
wars.outcome: Owain proclaimed Prince of Wales 16 September 1400; most of Wales held from 1404; Aberystwyth regained by 1408, Harlech in winter 1408-1409; Owain last seen in 1412.

certainty.note: Counties were defined in 1284 by the Statute of Rhuddlan; the March frontier is soft.

notes: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Gwynedd row runs to 1284 (the Gwynedd dossier ends it 1283); the Welsh principality of Llywelyn ap Gruffudd 1267-1283 ('Client kingdom (1267-1283)' in the infobox) is recorded in the Gwynedd dossier, so this dossier covers the English Principality only. The 1301 grant of 'all the lands under royal control in Wales' to the future Edward II (7 February 1301) moved no border. Typed colony: 'Dependent territory of England'. The counterparts used for the Glyndwr years are the rebel dossier glyndwr-s-wales. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] After the review: (1) the single 1283-1541 shape is split: whole 1283-1403, nothing 1404-1406 (the whole Principality is glyndwr-s-wales' in those years), Anglesey and Carmarthenshire 1407-1408, whole again from 1409, with gains mirroring the rebel losses (Anglesey late 1406, Carmarthenshire by 1407, Ceredigion 1408, Gwynedd and Conwy February 1409); (2) Flintshire is dropped (Principality page: created from the lordships of Tegeingl, Hopedale and Maelor Saesneg and administered with the Palatinate of Cheshire); (3) the 1283 gain of Ceredigion and Carmarthenshire from deheubarth stands because deheubarth now keeps Ceredigion in 1197-1282. English-held castles that held out in 1404-1406 are not drawn. kingdom-of-gwynedd dissolves in 1283/6 naming kingdom-of-england, not this state; its owner should read it as this state.
